item.content:encoded:
The picture of the underground lake is stunning and I was pretty interested to learn about cooking for vampires, but I didn't enjoy the characterization.

+ show block
– hide block

I kept being pulled out my enjoyment at the beginning by the inconsistent tone of the in-universe author. Sometimes they sound like an ancient vampire:

I have stayed in many hotels in my long unlife, many which have catered exclusively to hemovores like myself.

The venue wants to feed us, and we want to eat! But how to make food that we are actually capable of consuming?

and other times they sound like a cooking YouTube channel.

Every part of the place is specifically designed to be a great experience for all hemovores to relax.

The solution Chaz came up with: just use a lot of blood in the cooking process. If the food is bloody enough, then we'll be able to eat it and keep it down.

I recommend leaning more into the old vampire speech because you mostly stick to that in the latter sections and it works.

Meanwhile hunt section isn't that exciting. It's slow, but because we're seeing it from the vampire's point of view, there's no tension to be heightened by the slower pace. You could introduce some by giving the human a chance to defend themselves, but I think you'd be better off just making the human sacrifice a willing employee of Ambrose's; then you can at least get interesting dialogue about what working under him is like.

The Chaz interview doesn't do anything to flesh out the idea of 'Chaz is a horrible sophisticated monster' more than the rest of the article or even the new Chaz articles do.

We've grown stale as a brand.

I decided I wanted to start pushing the envelope, breaking new ground.

There was plenty of room to expand, innovate and start trying new material. I could finally break free of my shell and start doing what I really wanted to do.

Lots of long hours in the kitchen. Got fairly messy at times.

These are all character traits we learned in Do You Like Huey Lewis and the News. We even already learned that he cooks with blood in that tale! I'd be much more interested to know why Chaz chose to become a vampire, that lifestyle requires dedication and I want to know how he juggles it with being a chef! Him knowing all that would also give the reveal that he's a regular dude way more punch. Right now, the paragraphs about Chaz walking into the light unscathed don't enhance and honestly just slow the reveal down. He doesn't feel enigmatic — he still feels like celebrity chef Hannibal Lecter.

item.content:encoded: I really appreciate the authenticity approach here by Ambrose. The fact that a lot of the experience originates from more conventional approaches than any sort of magical solution (save for the desecration bit) really sells me on the piece. Every detail of the hotel was taken into consideration when crafting this as a haven for vampires, and it really shines in this format.
